summary: Anil Kumar works in computational linguistics and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Hyderabad by 2012 and held a post there.

Anil Vidyalankar is a scholar of linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, Columbia University, and the University of Delhi (PhD). He founded Sandhaan in 1988, serving as its Director (attested 1999).

Animesh Prakash works in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning an MA from the University of Hong Kong (2016–2017). He served as an Assistant Professor at Somaiya Vidyavihar University (2014–2018) and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (2018).

Animesh Roy focuses on Indology and philosophy. He completed an integrated MA in Sanskrit specializing in Advaita Vedanta at RKMVERI (2017–2022) and became a Research Scholar at Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit in 2022.
Animisha Tewari is an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned a BA from Miranda House (2017–2020) and an MA from the University of Delhi (2020–2022).

Anirban Dash works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. At the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, he served as a Research Assistant (attested 2003–2005) and later as Associate Professor of Sanskrit (attested 2026).
Anita is an Indologist who earned her Ph.D. from the University of Lucknow. She was a professor at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith in 2009.

Anjay Dhanawade studied history, archaeology, and Indology, earning a BA from the University of Mumbai (1996–1999), an MA from Savitribai Phule Pune University (2000–2002), and a Ph.D. from Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (2010–2016). He taught at Lokavikas Samajik Sanstha (2010–2023).
Ankita Chakraborty is an Indologist who studied under doctoral supervisor Bijoya Goswami (attested 2026). She served as a Research Scholar/Fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).
Ankita Nanda specializes in Indology. She completed her Ph.D. at Panjab University in 2022 and served there as a Senior Research Scholar the same year.

Ankur Barua works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at MAHE (MD 2003), Sikkim Manipal University (MBAIT 2007), and the University of Hong Kong (MBuddStud 2009) under Dorothy C. Wong, later holding an attested post at the University of Delhi (2012).

Ann Appleby Hazlewood is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned a Master of Arts at the Australian National University (attested 1983), studying under supervisors Tissa Rajapatirana and Luise Hercus.
Ann Gleig works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Rice University under the doctoral supervision of Jeffrey J. Kripal (attested 2010).

Ann Grodzins Gold is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She earned her BA, MA, and PhD in anthropology at the University of Chicago (~1973–1984), subsequently holding posts at Cornell University (~1988–1993) and Syracuse University (~1993–2021).
Ann Heirman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who taught Tom De Rauw and Ang Zou. She held posts at the National Fund for Scientific Research (1995–2009) and Ghent University (2003–2012).

Ann Laura Stoler is a historian who studied at Barnard College (BA ~1968–1972) and Columbia University (MA ~1972–1976). She taught at UW–Madison (1983–1989) and University of Michigan (1989–2004), and became founding director at The New School (2004).
Anna Andreeva is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She held a post at Heidelberg University and is attested as a permanent member at Ghent University in 2026.

Anna Aurelia Esposito is an Indologist who studied at Tübingen (MA 1998), Heidelberg, and Würzburg. She was an assistant professor at the University of Würzburg (attested 2012–2015) and held a post at the University of Zurich (attested 2026).

Anna Balikci-Denjongpa specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned a PhD from SOAS (2002) under Lionel Caplan, also studying with Lopen Dugyal and Gorlok Tulku, and held posts at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and Bulletin of Tibetology.

Anna Brown is a scholar of religious studies who was a Zen student under Robert Kennedy. Attested in 2017, she served at Saint Peter's University as political science department chair and social justice program director.
